question_text: The chemical oxygen generator is a system:1. which is inexpensive2. requiring no external input3. which is lightweight4. requiring no maintenance5. with adjustable flow rate6. which is unsafeThe combination regrouping all the correct statements is:
explanation: Chemical oxygen generators are widely used for passenger systems because they are lightweight, occupy minimal space, are relatively inexpensive, and require virtually no maintenance.

question_text: Consider the flight deck oxygen supply system. The purpose of the oxygen regulator (as a function of demand and altitude) is to:1. decrease oxygen pressure from 1800 PSI (in the bottles) down to about 50-75 PSI (low pressure system)2. supply pure oxygen3. supply diluted oxygen4. supply oxygen at normal pressure5. supply oxygen at emergency/positive pressure6. trigger the continuous cabin altitude warning at 10000 ft cabin altitudeThe combination regrouping all the correct statements is:
explanation: The flight deck diluter-demand regulator adjusts the oxygen supply based on cabin altitude and breathing rate. It is designed to deliver pure oxygen when selected, supply diluted oxygen mixed with cabin air, and provide oxygen at positive pressure.

question_text: A public transport aircraft is operated at FL 390. The total number of oxygen dispensing units and outlets in the cabin must be at least the same as the total number of :
option_a: seats exceeded by 10%.
option_c: passengers.
option_d: passengers exceeded by 10%.
explanation: Under airworthiness regulations for flight at high altitudes, the number of oxygen dispensing units (outlets and masks) in the passenger cabin must exceed the total number of passenger seats by at least 10% to ensure coverage for infants and mobile cabin crew.

question_text: A public transport aircraft has a cruising altitude of FL 390. It is fitted with individual oxygen masks for the passengers. In the event of depressurisation, the masks must be automatically released before the cabin pressure altitude exceeds:
explanation: In the event of a cabin depressurization, the automatic mask deployment system in the passenger cabin must release the masks from the overhead compartments before the cabin pressure altitude reaches 14,000 feet.

question_text: Above what flight level must one pilot wear an oxygen mask at all times during commercial flight.
explanation: Under commercial aviation operating rules, if a pressurized aircraft is operated above Flight Level 410 (FL 410), one pilot at the controls must wear and use an oxygen mask at all times, even if the other pilot has a quick-donning mask.

question_text: A diluter demand oxygen regulator :
option_a: delivers oxygen flow when inhaling.
option_b: delivers oxygen flow only above FL 100.
option_c: is only recommended for use with smoke in the cockpit.
option_d: mixes air and oxygen in a passenger oxygen mask.
explanation: A diluter-demand oxygen regulator is designed to deliver oxygen flow only during inhalation (demand). It also dilutes the oxygen with ambient cabin air at lower cabin altitudes to conserve the oxygen supply.

question_text: A jet aircraft is certified for the carriage of 120 passengers. 42 passenger are on board and the expected Flight Level on route Paris-Alger is FL 330. The first aid oxygen to be on board at departure shall provide breathing supply for at least:
option_a: 1 passenger for the entire flight after cabin depressurization at cabin altitude of more than 8000 ft.
option_c: 1 passenger for the entire flight after cabin depressurization at cabin altitude between 10000 and 14000 ft.
option_d: 3 passengers for the entire flight after cabin depressurization at cabin altitude between 10000 and 14000 ft.
explanation: Under operating regulations, first-aid (therapeutic) oxygen is required for pressurized aircraft operating above FL 250 to assist passengers who may suffer from hypoxia after a decompression. The system must provide enough oxygen for at least 2% of the passenger seats (or 1 passenger, whichever is greater) for the entire flight duration after depressurization when the cabin altitude exceeds 8,000 feet.

question_text: As regards passengers oxygen in public transport aircraft, information must be given to passengers through a demonstration. If a flight is to be carried out at Flight Level FL 290, this demonstration must be completed before :
option_a: take-off.
option_c: the aircraft reaches FL 140.
option_d: the aircraft reaches FL 250.
explanation: For any flight operating at altitudes where oxygen is required in the event of depressurization (above FL 250), the safety demonstration explaining the location and use of the passenger oxygen masks must be completed before takeoff.

question_text: In jet transport aircraft, breathing oxygen for the cockpit is stored in the following state:
option_a: gaseous.
option_c: chemical.
option_d: chemical or gaseous.
explanation: In commercial jet transport aircraft, the breathing oxygen for the cockpit crew is stored in high-pressure cylinders in its gaseous state. This allows the diluter-demand system to function properly, unlike the chemical generators typically used for passengers.

question_text: Oxygen systems are systems used on pressurized airplanes in :1. an emergency in the case of depressurization.2. an emergency in the case of the indisposition of a passenger.3. normal use in order to supply oxygen to the cabin.5. an emergency in the case of smoke or toxic gases.The combination regrouping all the correct statements is:
explanation: Oxygen systems on pressurized airplanes are emergency systems. They are used in the event of cabin depressurization (to prevent hypoxia) and in cases of cockpit smoke or toxic gases (to protect the flight crew).

question_text: Modern pressurized transport airplanes are equipped with :
option_a: two independent oxygen systems, one supplying the cockpit, the other the cabin.
option_b: only one oxygen system supplying the whole aircraft.
option_c: two oxygen systems both supplying the cockpit and the cabin.
option_d: only portable oxygen bottles.
explanation: Pressurized commercial transports utilize two completely independent oxygen systems. The flight crew is supplied by a high-pressure gaseous oxygen cylinder system, while the passenger cabin is supplied either by chemical oxygen generators or a separate gaseous distribution system.

question_text: Generally speaking when the oxygen flows to the masks in the passenger cabin, the system is activated by
option_a: firmly pulling the mask towards the face, after the cover has opened.
option_b: activating the relevant switch in the cockpit.
option_c: firmly pulling the cover behind which the oxygen mask is stowed.
option_d: pushing the mask against the face and breath normally.
explanation: When the passenger oxygen masks drop from the overhead panels, the oxygen flow does not start automatically. The passenger must pull the mask firmly toward them, which pulls a release cord that triggers the chemical generator firing pin or opens the supply valve.

question_text: A pressurized aeroplane is operated at FL 300. It undergoes a rapid decompression so that the pressure in the cabin goes quickly down to the outside pressure value. What happens concerning the oxygen system ?
option_a: the oxygen masks are automatically presented to cabin crew members and passengers
option_b: the oxygen masks are automatically presented to flight crew members
option_c: if the automatic mask presentation has been activated, the oxygen will flow within the first 3 minutes
option_d: manual override of the automatic presentation of passenger oxygen masks is, generally speaking, not possible
explanation: In the event of a rapid cabin decompression at FL 300, the cabin altitude pressure will rise quickly. An automatic barometric switch will trigger, releasing the mask compartment doors and presenting the passenger oxygen masks to all passengers and cabin crew.

question_text: A substance which may never be used in the vicinity or on parts of an oxygen installation is :
option_a: Grease
option_c: Halon
option_d: Nitrogen
explanation: Grease, oil, or any petroleum-based lubricants must never be used on or near oxygen system components. Pressurized pure oxygen can react violently and cause spontaneous, explosive combustion when it comes into contact with hydrocarbons.

question_text: The type of a aircraft oxygen system intended for use by passengers, is mostly :
option_a: a continuous flow system
option_c: portable equipment only
option_d: an air recycle system
explanation: The oxygen system installed for passengers in the cabin is typically a continuous flow system. This is the simplest and most lightweight method of delivering oxygen to a large number of occupants during an emergency descent.

question_text: The demand valve of a diluter-demand type oxygen regulator in normal mode, operates when the :
option_a: user breathes in
option_b: diluter control is in normal position
option_c: user requires 100 percent oxygen
option_d: pressure in the oxygen reservoir is more than 500 psi
explanation: The demand valve within a diluter-demand regulator is actuated by the suction created when the user inhales. This design ensures that oxygen only flows during inhalation, preventing waste of the gas supply.

question_text: The purpose of the ""Pressure Relief Valve"" in a high pressure oxygen system is to :
option_a: relieve overpressure if the pressure reducing valve malfunctions
option_b: reduce pressure in the oxygen reservoir to a suitable manifold pressure for the regulator
option_c: act as a manual shut-off valve
option_d: maximize the charging pressure of the system
explanation: The purpose of a pressure relief valve in a high-pressure oxygen system is to prevent damage to the downstream low-pressure components. In the event of a pressure regulator failure, the relief valve vents the excess pressure overboard.

question_text: The purpose of the first aid oxygen is to:
option_a: provide some passengers with additional respiratory assistance after an emergency descent following a depressurization.
option_b: provide the cabin attendants with respiratory protection.
option_c: supply all the passengers in case of depressurization.
option_d: provide the flight crew with respiratory assistance after depressurization.
explanation: First-aid (therapeutic) oxygen is carried to provide respiratory assistance to passengers who continue to experience breathing difficulties or pathological symptoms following an emergency descent after a decompression.

question_text: The survival oxygen is:
option_a: the oxygen supplied to the airplane occupants in case of accidental depressurization.
option_b: the oxygen supplied to a passenger who needs oxygen for pathological reasons.
option_c: the oxygen used for protection against smoke and carbon dioxide.
option_d: a therapeutical oxygen specifically carried for certain passengers.
explanation: Survival oxygen is the regulatory term for the emergency oxygen supply provided to the passengers and crew of an aircraft to prevent hypoxia during and after a cabin depressurization.

question_text: Airliners are equipped with oxygen systems. It can be said that :
option_a: with setting on ""NORMAL"", the crew breathes a mixture of oxygen / cabin air.
option_b: the same circuit is used by the crew and the passengers.
option_c: the seals must be carefully greased to avoid sparks.
option_d: the passenger circuit never uses chemically generated oxygen.
explanation: When the cockpit oxygen regulator is set to "NORMAL," it functions as a diluter-demand regulator. It automatically increases the proportion of pure oxygen in the inhaled mixture as the cabin altitude increases to maintain adequate blood oxygen saturation.

question_text: An oxygen regulator has 3 controls :- a power lever : ON/OFF- an ""O2"" lever : NORMAL/100%- an emergency lever : ON/OFFAmong the following statements, the correct proposition is :
option_a: the power lever on ON, and, the ""O2"" lever on NORMAL allows the oxygen to enter the regulator and enables breathing of a mixture of air/oxygen according to altitude.
option_b: the EMERGENCY lever on ON enables breathing of pure oxygen at ambient pressure.
option_c: the ""O2"" lever on ON enables breathing of the over-pressure oxygen at a constant flow rate.
option_d: with the EMERGENCY lever on OFF, in an emergency situation, one cannot use the oxygen mask to breathe.
explanation: The cockpit oxygen regulator controls are designed so that placing the power lever to "ON" and the "O2" lever to "NORMAL" opens the oxygen supply and delivers a diluted oxygen/air mixture that automatically varies with cabin altitude.

question_text: The operations of an airline plan the operation of a pressurized aircraft at a 240 flight level on its whole route with 150 passengers on board.As concerns the regulatory requirements about oxygen:1. each crew member will have available a quick fitting inhaler device.2. the aircraft will be equipped with a warning system indicating that the cabin altitude is higher than 3 000 m.3 . the quantity of oxygen on board will be sufficient for the supply of 100 % of the occupants during the whole flight time above the flight level 150 after an eventual depressurization.4. the first aid quantity of oxygen will be sufficient for the supply of two passengers during the whole flight time when the cabin altitude is greater than 8 000 feet.The combination regrouping all the correct statements is:
explanation: For a flight at FL 240, the aircraft must be equipped with an automatic aural or visual warning system to alert the crew if the cabin pressure altitude exceeds 10,000 feet. Additionally, survival oxygen must be sufficient to supply all passengers during the portion of the flight above FL 150.

question_text: When selected to normal, the oxygen proportion of the air/oxygen mixture supplied by the cockpit oxygen system regulator:
option_a: increases when the altitude increases.
option_c: is constant whatever the altitude.
explanation: When the cockpit oxygen regulator is set to "NORMAL," it functions as a diluter-demand regulator. It automatically increases the proportion of pure oxygen in the inhaled mixture as the cabin altitude increases to maintain adequate blood oxygen saturation.

question_text: In the cabin, when the oxygen mask is pulled downwards, the passenger breathes :
option_a: a mixture of oxygen and cabin air.
option_c: pure oxygen at the ambient pressure.
option_d: cabin air under pressure.
explanation: When a passenger pulls down the oxygen mask and places it over their face, they breathe a mixture of pure oxygen from the reservoir bag and ambient cabin air that enters through thin diluter valves on the mask shell.

question_text: Chemical oxygen generators are used to furnish oxygen to the :
option_a: cabin only.
option_c: cockpit only.
option_d: toilets only.
explanation: Chemical oxygen generators are used exclusively for the passenger cabin and lavatories. They are not used for the cockpit crew, who require demand regulators and the ability to breathe 100% oxygen or positive pressure in the event of smoke.

question_text: The chemical oxygen generator supplies oxygen for about :
option_a: 15 minutes.
option_c: 2 hours.
option_d: 5 minutes.
explanation: Chemical oxygen generators are designed to produce a continuous flow of oxygen for approximately 15 minutes. This duration is sufficient to cover a standard emergency descent to a safe breathing altitude of 10,000 feet.

question_text: The advantages of a chemical oxygen source for the passenger cabin are :1. reduced weight and volume,2. easy storage and maintenance,3. greater autonomy,4. no risk of explosion,5. reversible functioning,6. no maintenance.The combination regrouping all the correct statements is:
explanation: Chemical oxygen generators offer significant advantages for the cabin, including low weight and volume, easy storage, no risk of high-pressure explosion (since the gas is only generated on use), and a maintenance-free service life.

question_text: The disadvantages of a chemical oxygen source for the passenger cabin are :1. a flow which cannot be modulated,2. a heavy and bulky system,3. non reversible functioning,4. risks of explosion,5. poor autonomy.The combination regrouping all the correct statements is:
explanation: The primary disadvantages of chemical oxygen generators are that the chemical reaction is non-reversible (once started, it cannot be stopped), the flow rate cannot be adjusted or modulated, and they generate significant heat during operation.

question_text: The advantages of a gaseous oxygen source for the passenger cabin are :1. a greater autonomy,2. no risk of explosion,3. reversible functioning,4. easy storage and maintenance,5. possibility to regulate flow.The combination regrouping all the correct statements is :
explanation: The advantages of using a gaseous oxygen system for the passenger cabin are that the gas supply can be shut off (reversible functioning), it offers potentially greater duration, and the flow rate can be modulated or regulated by the system valves.

question_text: When the door operation of a transport airplane equipped with evacuation slides is controlled from the outside, the slide:
option_a: is disarmed automatically.
option_c: unfolds but does not become inflated.
option_d: becomes inflated in its packboard thus preventing its unfolding.
explanation: On transport aircraft, if a passenger door is opened from the outside, the door mechanical linkage automatically disarms the escape slide. This safety feature prevents the slide from accidentally inflating and blocking rescue personnel.

question_text: The equipment of an oxygen supply installation must be kept absolutely free of oil or grease traces as:
option_a: these substances catch fire spontaneously in the presence of oxygen under pressure.
option_b: the oxygen system would be contaminated.
option_c: these substances mixed with oxygen could catch fire in the presence of a spark.
option_d: these substances could plug the oxygen masks filters.
explanation: Pressurized pure oxygen acts as a powerful oxidizer. High-pressure oxygen in contact with even minute traces of oil or grease can trigger an immediate, highly explosive spontaneous chemical reaction.

question_text: A passenger emergency mask is a :
option_a: continuous flow mask and cannot be used if there is smoke in the cabin.
option_b: mask with flow on request and cannot be used if there is smoke in the cabin.
option_c: continuous flow mask and can be used if there is smoke in the cabin.
option_d: mask with flow on request and can be used if there is smoke.
explanation: The standard passenger emergency oxygen mask is a continuous flow rebreather mask. Because it dilutes the oxygen with ambient cabin air drawn through open valves, it cannot protect the user if the cabin is filled with smoke or toxic fumes.

question_text: A smoke mask is a :
option_a: mask with flow on request and covers the whole face.
option_b: continuous flow mask and covers the whole face.
option_c: mask with flow on request and covers only the nose and the mouth.
option_d: continuous flow mask and covers only the nose and the mouth.
explanation: A protective smoke mask (or full-face mask) is a demand-type mask that covers the user's entire face (including the eyes). This design protects the eyes and respiratory system from smoke, fumes, and noxious gases in the cockpit.

question_text: In accordance with JAR-OPS 1, each occupant of the cockpit seats on duty in a non-pressurized airplane must have an oxygen supply reserve for the entire flight time at pressure altitudes greater than:
explanation: In non-pressurized aircraft, operating regulations state that the flight crew must use supplemental oxygen for the entire duration of the flight at pressure altitudes above 10,000 feet.

question_text: In accordance with JAR-OPS 1, 100 % of the passengers in a non-pressurized airplane must have an oxygen supply reserve for the entire flight time at pressure altitudes greater than:
explanation: In non-pressurized aircraft, all passengers must be supplied with supplemental oxygen for the entire flight time spent at pressure altitudes above 13,000 feet.

question_text: In accordance with JAR-OPS 1, 10 % of the passengers in a non-pressurized airplane must have an oxygen supply reserve for the entire flight time when the cabin altitude pressure is greater than:
option_a: 10000 ft but not exceeding 13000 ft minus 30 minutes.
option_d: 10000 ft but not exceeding 13000 ft.
explanation: For flights in non-pressurized aircraft, at least 10% of the passengers must be provided with supplemental oxygen for any flight duration exceeding 30 minutes at altitudes between 10,000 feet and 13,000 feet.

question_text: In accordance with JAR-OPS 1, when an airplane flies at over 25000 ft, the total number of oxygen dispensing units and supply terminals must be at least greater than the number of:
option_a: seats by 10 %.
option_c: seats by 30 %.
option_d: passengers by 30%.
explanation: For aircraft certified to operate at cruise altitudes above 25,000 feet, the number of oxygen dispensing units (masks and outlets) installed in the passenger cabin must exceed the number of passenger seats by at least 10%.

question_text: In case of smoke in the cockpit, the crew oxygen regulator must be set to:
option_c: emergency.
option_d: on demand.
explanation: In the event of smoke, fumes, or toxic gases in the cockpit, the flight crew must set their oxygen regulators to the "EMERGENCY" position. This delivers 100% oxygen under positive pressure, preventing contaminated cabin air from leaking into the mask.

question_text: The installation and use of on-board oxygen generators is such that:1 - the smoking ban is imperative when used2 - in case of accidental drop of the ""continuous flow"" passenger masks, no crew action is required3 - no trace of grease must be found in the system assembly4 - the system's filling adaptors must be greased with non freezable or graphite greaseThe combination which regroups all of the correct statements is :
option_a: 03-Jan
option_c: 03-Fev
option_d: 04-Fev
explanation: The safety regulations for oxygen systems state that smoking must be strictly banned when oxygen is in use, and no traces of grease or hydrocarbons are allowed anywhere in the system assembly.

question_text: In a pressurized transport aircraft, the protective breathing equipment:
option_a: protects the members of the crew against fumes and noxious gases.
option_b: gives medical assistance to certain passengers with respiratory disorders.
option_c: protects all the occupants against the effects of accidental depressurization.
option_d: protects the members of the crew against the effects of accidental depressurization.
explanation: Protective Breathing Equipment (PBE), such as smoke hoods, is designed to protect the flight crew and cabin crew members against the physiological hazards of dense smoke, toxic fumes, and noxious gases while fighting fires.

question_text: An operator shall not operate an aeroplane certicated to JAR25, across an area in which search and rescue would be especially difficult, without survival equipment if it flies away from an area suitable for making an emergency landing at a distance greater than :
option_a: 90 minutes at cruising speed.
option_c: 30 minutes at cruising speed.
option_d: 120 minutes at cruising speed.
explanation: Under operating rules, an aircraft must carry emergency survival equipment (such as rafts and beacons) when flying over areas where search and rescue would be difficult, if it operates more than 90 minutes flying time from a suitable landing area.

question_text: A turboprop aeroplane is performing an overwater flight, which takes it further than 340 NM away from an aerodrome where an emergency landing could be performed. Normal cruising speed is 180 kt. One engine out airspeed is 155 kt.
option_a: Life jackets must be available for all occupants.
option_b: The regulation does not require life jackets or rafts to be taken on board in this particular case.
option_c: Life jackets and rafts must be available for all occupants.
option_d: Life rafts must be available for all occupants.
explanation: For multi-engine aircraft, if the flight path takes it more than 120 minutes at cruising speed or 400 NM away from a suitable landing field, it must carry life rafts and life jackets for all occupants. In this case, since the aircraft is flying further than 340 NM, life jackets must be available for all occupants.

question_text: The number of hand fire extinguishers which have to be installed in the passenger cabin according to JAR-OPS depends on the number of :
option_a: seats in the cabin.
option_c: passengers in the cabin.
option_d: emergency exits in the cabin.
explanation: The number of hand-held fire extinguishers required to be installed in the passenger compartment of a commercial transport aircraft is determined directly by the number of passenger seats installed in the cabin.

question_text: The crash/fire axe is part of the safety equipment fitted to passenger aircraft. Its function is to :
option_a: obtain forced access to a fire behind a panel and a general purpose tool during evacuation.
option_b: free exits in case of evacuation via the sides.
option_c: activate a radio survival beacon by cutting off the red coloured top
option_d: settle an escalating conflict with unreasonable passengers, who threaten flight safety.
explanation: The primary function of the crash axe stored in the cockpit is to allow the flight crew to chop through internal panels, sidewalls, or cabin linings to locate and extinguish hidden fires, and to serve as a general-purpose tool during emergency evacuations.

question_text: In accordance with the JAR-OPS, an airplane constituted of only one passenger deck, equipped with 61 seats and effectively carrying passengers, must be equipped with :
option_a: 1 megaphone.
option_c: 2 megaphones if there are more than 31 passengers on board.
option_d: no megaphone.
explanation: Under operating regulations, passenger aircraft with a seating capacity of 61 to 99 seats must be equipped with at least 1 portable battery-powered megaphone to assist the crew in directing an evacuation.

question_text: In accordance with the JAR-OPS and with the exception of amphibians and hydroplanes, the carriage of a life jacket per person on board is compulsory when the airplane is :1. cruising at such a distance from the shore that it would not be able to return in the case of an engine failure.2. is flying over a water surface at more than 50 NM off shore.3. is using departure and arrival paths above the water and when a ditching probability exists in the case of a problem.4. is flying over a stretch of water at more than 100 NM off shore.The combination regrouping all the correct statements is:
explanation: For landplanes, carrying a life jacket for each occupant is compulsory when the aircraft is operating more than 50 NM from the shore, or when taking off or landing at an airport where the departure or arrival path is over water and a ditching risk exists.

question_text: The number of manual fire-extinguishers, on board the passenger cabin of an airplane, whose maximum approved configuration for passenger seats is 31, is:
explanation: Under operating regulations, an aircraft with a passenger seating configuration of 31 to 60 seats must be equipped with a minimum of 2 hand-held fire extinguishers in the passenger cabin.

question_text: The number of crash axes on board an airplane, whose maximum approved configuration of passenger seats is 201, is :
explanation: For aircraft with a maximum passenger seating configuration exceeding 200 seats, operating regulations require a minimum of 2 crash axes or crowbars to be carried on board.

question_text: A public transport passengers aircraft, with a seating configuration of more than 61 seats, must have in its passenger compartment(s), at least 3 portable fire- extinguishers including:
option_a: 2 halon fire-extinguishers.
option_c: 3 halon fire-extinguishers.
option_d: no halon fire-extinguisher.
explanation: For passenger cabins configured with more than 61 seats, the regulations require that at least 2 of the installed hand-held fire extinguishers utilize Halon 1211 as the extinguishing agent.

question_text: In a ditching situation, the passenger life jackets will be inflated :
option_a: when leaving the airplane.
option_b: immediately on the opening of the exits.
option_c: immediately on ditching.
option_d: once the passengers are in the water.
explanation: In a ditching situation, passengers must never inflate their life jackets inside the aircraft cabin, as this would restrict movement and block the exits. The jackets must only be inflated when leaving the airplane.

question_text: An aircraft whose maximum approved configuration for passenger seats is 10 seats must be equipped with:
option_a: one fire-extinguisher in the cockpit and three fire-extinguishers in the passenger cabin.
option_b: one fire-extinguisher in the cockpit and two fire- extinguishers in the passenger cabin.
option_c: three fire-extinguishers in the passenger cabin only.
option_d: two fire-extinguishers in the cockpit and two fire-extinguishers in the passenger cabin.
explanation: For an aircraft configured with 10 passenger seats, safety regulations require the installation of 1 hand-held fire extinguisher in the cockpit for the flight crew, and at least 2 hand-held fire extinguishers in the passenger cabin.

question_text: There are 60 passengers and crew members on board a turbo-prop aircraft. Its speed is 240 kt. At a point along the course steered, above the sea, the aircraft is at 1h45 min from an airdrome suitable for emergency landing. The minimum equipment complying with regulations is :
option_a: 60 life jackets and three 30-seat life boats
option_c: One 30-seat life boat and two 20-seat life boats
option_d: 60 life jackets, two 30-seat life boats
explanation: Because the aircraft is operating further than 120 minutes or 400 NM from a suitable landing airfield, it must carry life rafts with sufficient capacity to accommodate all 60 occupants. This requires 60 life jackets and at least two 30-seat life rafts.

question_text: The emergency lighting system must be able to function and supply a certain level of lighting after the main electric power system has been cut off for at least:
option_a: 10 minutes
option_c: 5 minutes
option_d: 30 minutes
explanation: The emergency lighting system must be equipped with an independent power source that can power the lights for at least 10 minutes after a complete loss of main aircraft electrical power.

question_text: An aircraft whose maximum approved configuration for passenger seats is 200 seats must be equipped with:
option_a: 3 manual fire-extinguishers in the passenger cabin.
option_b: 5 manual-fire extinguishers in the passenger cabin.
option_c: 7 manual-fire extinguishers in the passenger cabin.
option_d: 4 manual fire-extinguishers in the passenger cabin.
explanation: Under operating regulations, an aircraft with a passenger seating configuration of 61 to 200 seats is required to have a minimum of 3 hand-held fire extinguishers distributed throughout the passenger cabin.

question_text: The pyrotechnic means used in case of an emergency to indicate your position to the emergency teams are a flare:
option_a: which is used at night and a smoke device which is used in the daytime.
option_b: and a smoke device which are only used at night.
option_c: which is used at daytime and a smoke device which is used at night.
option_d: and a smoke device which are only used in the daytime.
explanation: Standard aircraft survival kits include dual-purpose pyrotechnic flares. The bright red flare is designed for nighttime signalling, while the orange smoke device is designed to create a highly visible plume during the daytime to guide rescue teams.

question_text: The portable emergency beacons which are used after an emergency landing or ditching have a duration of :
explanation: Portable Emergency Locator Transmitters (ELTs) or survival beacons designed for use after an emergency landing or ditching are required by regulations to have a battery capacity that supports continuous transmission on emergency frequencies for at least 48 hours.

question_text: In accordance with JAR-OPS 1 and if necessary, the number of liferafts to be found on board an aircraft must allow the transportation of the entire aircraft occupants:
option_a: in the case of a loss of one raft of the largest rated capacity.
option_c: plus 30 %.
option_d: in the case of a loss of two rafts.
explanation: To ensure passenger safety during a ditching, operating regulations dictate that the total capacity of the life rafts carried on board must be sufficient to transport all aircraft occupants even in the event of the loss of the single largest capacity raft.
